prayerExcerpt.en-US: His vigilance protected his flock from the wiles of the heretics Valentine and Marcion.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Sua vigilância protegeu seu rebanho das astúcias dos hereges Valentim e Marcião.

meta.face: A Syrian of Emesa, about sixty-five, with a warm, olive-brown complexion and a TALL, NARROW, EGG-SHAPED head, broadest across the upper face — a high, SLOPING forehead, a LONG, THIN, gently ARCHED nose with a narrow bridge, LARGE, dark, luminous eyes with HEAVY LOWER LIDS under THICK, black-and-grey brows that ARCH HIGH toward the temples, lean cheeks, NOTICEABLY FULL, wide lips; black-and-grey hair CROPPED VERY SHORT, close to the skull; a long, full, gently curling black beard streaked with grey, falling to the breast; the gaze watchful and grave, toward us.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. Wikipedia (after the Liber Pontificalis) makes him a Syrian of Emesa who decreed that clergy should not wear long hair, and records Polycarp's visit over the Easter question; its lead image is a Baroque statue of an old, bearded pope. The book tells the same visit and his vigilance against Valentine and Marcion; its engraving shows him seated with a standing visitor. The cropped hair follows the decree; the narrow, egg-shaped face with the full lips and high-arched brows is our choice.
